title: Branches of science
competency: Describe the main branches of science and explain how the natural sciences overlap.

keywords.def: The study of nature and natural laws. Its main branches are biology, chemistry and physics.
The other major category of science. It studies people and human society.
The branch of natural science that studies living things.
The branch of natural science about the properties, make-up, structure and changes of substances.
The branch of natural science that studies matter, energy and how they interact.
Biology and physics combined: the study of physical processes in living things, from molecules to whole organisms.
Biology and chemistry combined: the study of chemical processes and reactions in living things.
Chemistry and physics combined: the study of the properties of materials and how they interact.

en.text: Science has two major categories: natural science and social science. Natural science studies nature and natural laws. Its three branches are biology, which studies living things, chemistry, which studies substances, and physics, which studies matter and energy.

am.text: ሳይንስ ሁለት ዋና ዋና ክፍሎች አሉት፤ የተፈጥሮ ሳይንስና ማህበራዊ ሳይንስ። የተፈጥሮ ሳይንስ ተፈጥሮንና የተፈጥሮ ሕጎችን ያጠናል። ሦስቱ ቅርንጫፎቹ ሥነ ሕይወት፣ ኬሚስትሪና ፊዚክስ ናቸው። ሥነ ሕይወት ሕያዋንን፣ ኬሚስትሪ ንጥረ ነገሮችን፣ ፊዚክስ ቁስና ኃይልን ያጠናሉ።

screens.title: Sort the questions
screens.text: Before you read, sort these questions. What is each one about?
items: How does a maize plant grow?
Why does an iron sheet roof rust?
Rusting changes one substance into another.
Why does a ball roll faster down a steep hill?
It is about motion and energy.
How does a cow digest grass?
What is table salt made of?
It is about the make-up of a substance.
How does sunlight warm a tin roof?

screens.title: Two major categories
paras: Science has two major categories: natural science and social science.
Natural science studies nature and natural laws. It includes chemistry, biology and physics.

screens.title: Three branches of natural science
items: Studies the properties, make-up, structure and changes of substances.
Studies matter and energy and how they interact.

screens.title: Name the branches
defs: The study of nature and natural laws.
The other major category. It studies people and human society.
The study of the properties, make-up, structure and changes of substances.

screens.title: Two categories
screens.why: Natural science and social science are the two major categories.
screens.clue: Look at the first split under "Science" in Figure 1.1.

screens.title: Chaltu's garden
screens.text: Chaltu studies how a maize plant grows in her school garden in Adama.
screens.why: A plant is a living thing, and biology studies living things.
screens.ask: Which branch of natural science is this?

screens.title: Matter and energy
screens.ask: The branch that studies matter, energy and how they interact is ___.
screens.why: That is the definition of physics.
screens.clue: Look at the three branches again.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: Chemistry deals with the properties, make-up, structure and changes of substances.
screens.why: That is how the book describes chemistry.

en.text: There is no clear border line between biology, chemistry and physics. Their knowledge overlaps. Biophysics joins biology and physics. Biochemistry joins biology and chemistry. Physical chemistry joins chemistry and physics.

am.text: በሥነ ሕይወት፣ በኬሚስትሪና በፊዚክስ መካከል ግልጽ ድንበር የለም። እውቀታቸው ይደራረባል። ባዮፊዚክስ ሥነ ሕይወትንና ፊዚክስን ያጣምራል። ባዮኬሚስትሪ ሥነ ሕይወትንና ኬሚስትሪን ያጣምራል። ፊዚካል ኬሚስትሪ ኬሚስትሪንና ፊዚክስን ያጣምራል።

screens.title: Two subjects at once?
screens.text: A doctor at Black Lion Hospital studies the tiny electric signals that make the heart beat.
screens.after: She needs both. The heart is alive, and electricity is physics. Sciences overlap.

screens.title: No clear border line
paras: There is no clear border line between the natural sciences. Their knowledge overlaps.
Chemistry and physics together are studied as physical science (physical chemistry). It studies the properties of materials and how they interact.

screens.caption: Figure 1.2 Where two sciences overlap, a new field is born.

screens.title: Fields that join two sciences
paras: Biophysics joins biology and physics. It studies life's physical processes, from molecules to cells, tissues and organisms.
Biochemistry joins biology and chemistry. It explores the chemical reactions inside living things.

screens.title: Name the joined fields
defs: Biology + physics: physical processes in living things.
Biology + chemistry: chemical processes and reactions in living things.
Chemistry + physics: the properties of materials and how they interact.

screens.title: Why they overlap
screens.text: Why do the branches of natural science overlap?
opts: They are all the same subject
Only physics is a real science
Scientists cannot decide which is which
There is no clear border line between them
screens.ans: There is no clear border line between them
screens.why: Their knowledge overlaps, so new fields combine two of them.
screens.clue: Read the first sentence of "No clear border line".

screens.title: Inside a cell
screens.text: Studying the physical processes inside living cells belongs to:
screens.why: Biophysics = biology + physics: physical processes in living things.
screens.clue: Which two circles does it join: living things and what else?

screens.title: Name the partner
screens.why: Bio- means life; the rest of the word tells you the second science.
screens.clue: Look at the second part of the word "biochemistry".

screens.title: Digesting injera
screens.text: Dawit studies the chemical reactions that break down injera in the stomach.
screens.why: Chemical reactions inside a living body belong to biochemistry.
screens.clue: Is it physical or chemical? Is it in a living thing?
screens.worked: The stomach is part of a living thing: biology. Breaking down food is a chemical reaction: chemistry. Biology + chemistry = biochemistry.

items.title: 1. What is science?
items.ask: Science is a systematic method of gaining knowledge, based on observation and ___.
items.why: Science is a systematic method of gaining knowledge about the physical and natural world and human society, based on observation and evidence.
items.clue: What do scientists collect to support an idea?

items.title: 2. Three branches
items.ask: The three branches of natural science are biology, chemistry and ___.
items.clue: Which branch studies matter and energy?

items.title: 3. Matter and energy
items.ask: The field of science that studies matter and energy is ___.
items.clue: It is one of the three branches of natural science.

items.title: 4. Biophysics or biochemistry?
items.text: What is the difference between biophysics and biochemistry?
opts: Biophysics studies physical processes in living things; biochemistry studies chemical processes in living things
Biophysics studies rocks; biochemistry studies stars
Biophysics studies chemical reactions; biochemistry studies energy only
items.ans: Biophysics studies physical processes in living things; biochemistry studies chemical processes in living things
items.why: Biophysics = biology + physics. Biochemistry = biology + chemistry.
items.clue: Look at the second part of each word.

test.text: Biology, physics and chemistry do not share any common areas of study.
test.why: There is no clear border line between them. Their knowledge overlaps.

test.text: A student studies the chemical reactions that happen inside the human body. Which field is this?
test.why: Biochemistry combines biology and chemistry: chemical processes in living things.

notes.text: Spelling slips in the printed book are corrected: "Biopysics" is biophysics, "boarder" is border.
The book gives no examples of social sciences. History, geography and economics are named in a side note only as common examples.
Exercise 1.1 is short-answer in the book. Questions 1–3 are turned into fill-in blanks and question 4 into a multiple choice, using the answers given in the source.
Figure 1.1 shows the branches as a tree. Social science studies people and human society. The book gives no examples; history, geography and economics are common ones.

Figure 1.2 is a Venn diagram of three circles: biology, physics and chemistry. Where two circles overlap, a new field is born. Spelling slips in the printed book are corrected here: "Biopysics" is biophysics, "boarder" is border.
